So I have seen a lot of posts that say to always use the package manager when installing stuff in Linux. I have Linux Mint 17.2 installed on my laptop and want to install the new Libre Office 5. I downloaded the tar.gz package and tried going to my synaptic package manager but I can't figure out how to add it in there for install? When I click add a downloaded package they are all greyed out. Can anyone give a quick tutorial on how I would go about this kind of thing?

tar.gz aren't packages, they are compressed file containers.

When people say to use your package manager, they mean to use your package manager to download and install the files.

Very rarely should you be downloading programs from websites. You should be having your package manager handle that for you.

You said used Synaptic. Just do a search in Synaptic for Libre Office, tick the checkbox, hit apply, wait and you are done.
This is exactly what I was looking for. Thanks.
